nodes.label: SESSION_AUTH: server-side cookie capture for social sources
nodes.rationale: Not 'unblock Instagram' and not 'unblock YouTube': it gives every source an optional per-user signed-in session so a rate-limited source degrades to 'reconnect your account' instead of a dead end. Capture is insurance against a currently dormant failure mode, which is why the cheap deterministic fixes are sequenced first.

nodes.label: jar (Netscape-format cookie file)
nodes.rationale: Netscape is the interchange format because it is what CDP Storage.getCookies maps onto cleanly and what yt-dlp --cookies consumes; storing two formats would double the secret surface and let them drift.

nodes.label: §1.1 YouTube GVS 403 (settled by measurement)
nodes.rationale: Metadata always resolves and only the media fetch 403s; the default client loses 3 of 6 videos while web_embedded wins 4 of 4. Cookies would not have fixed it because a GVS 403 is a SABR/PO-token-tier refusal, not an auth challenge. The list of working clients is a moving target set by YouTube, which is why it belongs in config and not a source file.

nodes.label: §1.1b PO tokens rejected
nodes.rationale: The provider's own docs say PO tokens do not guarantee bypassing 403s or bot checks, and bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider needs Node.js >=20 or Deno, colliding with the Bun-first rule at the moment Branch A is trying to remove Python. Kept as a documented escalation only.

nodes.label: §1.2 Instagram consolidation hypothesis (blocked on proof)
nodes.rationale: If yt-dlp --cookies works with a real signed-in jar, both sources collapse onto one downloader and Python leaves the image. 'Cookies are required' is proven (the extractor names --cookies itself); 'cookies are sufficient' is not (open issues report empty media responses). Experiment (c) decides it: if yt-dlp's extractor returns a null or junk title, agent routing silently degrades on every Reel -- plausible wrong output rather than an error, the worst failure mode in this codebase.

nodes.label: Branch A: yt-dlp-only consolidation
nodes.rationale: Deletes instaloader.ts and its binary spec, drops python3/pip and INSTALOADER_* from the Dockerfile, and restores the deliberately Python-free slim base; the sources[] machinery is kept because it is correct and costs nothing.

nodes.label: Branch B: instaloader stays, session derived per run
nodes.rationale: instaloader consumes its own pickled session keyed to a username, so Netscape stays canonical and a tiny adapter materializes instaloader's form inside the run's temp dir and dies with it -- one canonical secret, one derived artifact.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable sequencing: consolidation lands last
nodes.rationale: Deleting the fallback downloader in the same change that introduces cookies makes a cookie bug and a consolidation bug indistinguishable; the stale-worker episode showed how expensive a correct-looking failure with old wording is.

nodes.label: §2.1 Capture runs in its own Bun process
nodes.rationale: Next.js App Router handlers cannot upgrade to WebSocket (hono/vercel's handle() returns a Response) and a live Chromium handle is long-lived state a request-scoped handler cannot own; it also makes the concurrency cap enforceable because an in-memory session Map is only authoritative if one process owns it.

nodes.label: §2.4 CaptureProvider registry (provider-generic)
nodes.rationale: The exact analogue of ray-providers.ts, with loginUrl, sessionCookies, cookieDomains and a mapAccount that must return generic account_* keys. The social vocabulary derives from MEDIA_SOURCES rather than a hand-written second list, so a social credential's provider IS the media source id and download-time lookup needs no mapping table.

nodes.label: A third provider list is required (gap in the deferred note)
nodes.rationale: credentialInputSchema.provider is z.enum(PROVIDER_IDS) derived from ALL_PROVIDERS, which contains neither instagram nor youtube, so a cookie credential would be rejected at the schema boundary today -- the claim that only the Drizzle enum and Zod schema were needed was incomplete.

nodes.label: §2.5 Capture routes (/capture/:provider, finish, cancel)
nodes.rationale: A status poll route exists so the UI can recover if the WebSocket drops; the socket itself lives on the capture service, not in Next.js.

nodes.label: §3 Storage model (column mapping for a cookie credential)
nodes.rationale: The whole Netscape jar is one AES-256-GCM encrypted string in access_token because the vault already treats it as an opaque secret, so no new crypto is needed; refresh_token is NULL because a social session has no refresh grant and re-auth is a full recapture.

nodes.label: §3.2 expires_at is a floor on uselessness
nodes.rationale: A session can be revoked server-side long before cookie expiry, so past-expiry means definitely dead (cheap, indexed) while future means only maybe alive -- the UI must render 'Connected as @handle' and never 'valid until X'.

nodes.label: §3.3 What must never enter meta_data
nodes.rationale: meta_data is plaintext on disk AND returned by the API, so no cookie value ever, not even a truncated prefix; cookie NAMES are fine and help diagnose a partial capture without decrypting. isSensitiveKey matching 'cookie' auto-redacts cookie_names if meta_data is ever logged -- defence in depth, not the primary control.

nodes.label: §3.4 Reconnect works with no new code
nodes.rationale: createCredential already replaces on (userId, provider, account_id) for non-api_key types, so reconnecting the same account updates in place and a second account creates a second row -- the desired behaviour inherited free.

nodes.label: §3.5 Migration: NONE (Drizzle enum is TypeScript-level)
nodes.rationale: The generated DDL is plain TEXT with no CHECK constraint, so adding 'cookie' changes types only; the proof step is that db:generate must produce no new migration file. Note the TRD's CHECK(type IN ('api_key','ray')) was never built -- the code has always used api_key/oauth and the schema is the truth.

nodes.label: §3.6 getSecretByType (vault widening)
nodes.rationale: getAccessToken filters only on (userId, provider) with no type filter or ordering, which becomes ambiguous the moment two credential types share a provider id; a sibling function is added rather than changing the signature, returning credentialId so the reject counter can be written back.

nodes.label: §4.2 withSourceCookies (materialize and destroy)
nodes.rationale: No credential yields null and the downloader omits --cookies entirely, byte-for-byte today's anonymous path -- which is what makes every phase independently shippable and instantly revertible. The jar is written chmod 600 inside the run's temp dir and deleted in a finally, with purge() as a second line of defence against a hard kill.

nodes.label: §4.2 Jar rotation write-back (--cookies is read-write)
nodes.rationale: yt-dlp dumps the refreshed jar back on exit, so reading it back and re-encrypting when changed is how a session stays alive for weeks instead of expiring on its original cookie lifetime; never log the diff, only rotated: true.

nodes.label: §4.2b YouTube's stricter cookie rules
nodes.rationale: Reopening a YouTube session in a browser rotates the refresh token and invalidates the exported jar, so the capture profile dir must be single-use by explicit invariant and the registry needs a per-provider settleUrl visited immediately before harvest. Concurrent use of one jar forks the rotation chain, and using a real account carries documented ban risk that the Connect dialog must state plainly.

nodes.label: §4.3 SESSION_EXPIRED rule (hinges on one bit of state)
nodes.rationale: If a jar was supplied and the failure is login-shaped it is not SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; the old message even advised signing in, useless advice to a user who already has. It is permanent, never carries stderr, and trips Reconnect only at two rejects because a single transient checkpoint should not nag a user whose session is fine.

nodes.label: §4.4 Capture logging allowlist
nodes.rationale: Only source, credential_id, cookie_count, rotated and session_state are permitted; the middleware logs both request and response bodies, so capture routes must never put jar material in either and /finish returns the masked credential only.

nodes.label: §5.1 Capture concurrency cap and teardown
nodes.rationale: On a 4GB VPS two 500MB sessions leave headroom for a download+ffmpeg burst; 3 would fit on paper and lose it. The idle timer is the real reclaimer, not the TTL. Deliberately no wait-queue (MVP-first): a queue for a 2-slot once-per-user resource is machinery without a customer and a spinner that might resolve in 10 minutes is worse than an honest 503. Seven teardown paths exist because a leaked Chromium is 500MB that never comes back.

nodes.label: §5.2 The screencast WebSocket is a remote-control channel
nodes.rationale: Browsers cannot set headers on a WebSocket constructor, so a single-use 60s query-string ticket is the correct shape; reusing the app session cookie would make the socket CSRF-reachable from any origin. Redemption is atomic GETDEL, ownership is re-checked, Origin is checked, frames are Zod-validated, navigation is fenced (otherwise it is an SSRF-shaped proxy with a keyboard attached), and no frame or key event is ever logged.

nodes.label: §5.5 No fixed frame rate, ack backpressure instead
nodes.rationale: screencastFrameAck requests the next frame only after the client acknowledges the last, so the stream self-throttles to the slowest link instead of guessing an fps.

nodes.label: §5.6 What breaks first at 10 / 100 / 1000 users
nodes.rationale: At 10 users the pinch is throughput, not memory. At 100 it is the shared egress IP well before RAM, because a per-credential budget protects an account from its own burst, not from its neighbours. At 1000 the single VPS goes and per-user fairness must move from a Dragonfly semaphore to real queue partitioning.

nodes.label: §6 Risks (datacenter IP fingerprinting, password transit, jar blast radius)
nodes.rationale: CDP attachment is itself a detection vector and is unmitigated by design choice, so it must be measured in Phase 2 rather than argued. The user's password transits the capture process's memory keystroke-by-keystroke and cannot be engineered away (sessionid is HttpOnly), so it must be stated in the Connect dialog. A jar is a bearer credential for a whole account, so disconnecting in Relay does not log the session out on the platform.

nodes.label: Risk #8: the yt-dlp pin is stale with no bump cadence
nodes.rationale: A hard pin gives reproducible extraction across deploys, but YouTube breaks extractors continuously, so a pin with no cadence is a slow-motion outage; the answer is a monthly bump with the client matrix as the acceptance test, never a floating tag, which trades a predictable problem for an unpredictable one.

nodes.label: §7 Phased build plan (Phases 0-6)
nodes.rationale: Each phase is independently shippable and revertible; Phase 6 is last because it is the only phase that REMOVES a working code path, and phases 1-5 are purely additive since withSourceCookies yields null with no credential stored.
